Industry best practices:
Structure and mechanics:
• Safety factor of at least 2 on structural parts (3 for a filled plastic under long-term load: creep)
• Finite element calculation or simulation of loaded parts, drop and impact cases included
• Tolerance analysis (worst case or RSS) on every critical fit
• Fillets, no sharp corner or notch in a loaded area (stress concentration)
• Molded parts: uniform wall thickness, ribs, draft, material chosen with its data sheet
• Fasteners: specified torque, thread-locker or washer, metal inserts in plastic
• Stability: low center of gravity, tilt test on an inclined plane according to the product standard
For any function:
• Purchased part: data sheet read in full, qualified supplier, second source identified
• Standard part (ISO, DIN) with its strength or precision class specified on the drawing
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of everyone
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field returns from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the CdCF (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance
